meta.source: Indicative figures blended from public sources (GuruFocus, StockAnalysis, Simply Wall St, Stockopedia, Kalkine, company results) as researched on 2026-09-10. P/E, yield and payout vary by source and methodology (trailing vs forward, and whether special dividends are counted). Not live — regenerate with screener.py for current data.
meta.disclaimer: General information only, not financial or investment advice. Figures are indicative and may be stale or revised. Dividend yield and payout ratio are shown as additional context, not as screening criteria. A payout ratio above 100% means the dividend exceeds earnings and may not be sustainable. Verify against a live source and consider your own circumstances before making any decision.

stocks.name: Helia Group
stocks.note: Lenders mortgage insurer — an underwriter, not a funds manager. Headline yields near 22% appear when special dividends are counted; ordinary yield is ~6%. New business is shrinking.

stocks.name: GrainCorp
stocks.note: Grain handling and processing. Earnings swing with the harvest, and the payout currently exceeds earnings.

stocks.name: Autosports Group
stocks.note: Prestige and luxury car dealerships. Forward P/E ~7.1; payout covered by earnings (44%) though cash payout is tighter at 86%.

stocks.name: MotorCycle Holdings
stocks.note: Motorcycle dealerships and parts. Payout well covered on both earnings (54%) and cash (22%); EPS forecast to grow.

stocks.name: Qantas Airways
stocks.note: Strong operating cash flow, but free cash flow swings with fleet capex. Dividend resumed recently, fully franked.

stocks.name: Harvey Norman
stocks.note: Just above the P/E<10 line on trailing earnings. Appears if you nudge the ceiling to 11.

stocks.name: Peter Warren Automotive
stocks.note: Another dealership group just over the line; earnings estimates have been cut recently.

stocks.name: McMillan Shakespeare
stocks.note: Novated leasing and salary packaging — a financial services business, not a funds manager. Above the P/E cutoff.

stocks.name: Acumentis Group
stocks.note: A valuation and advisory services business, NOT a property trust — so it clears the REIT filter as intended. Fails only on P/E at 14.4; payout is comfortable at 34% of earnings. Appears if the ceiling goes to 15.
